Description & Mechanical Cause: Request URL not found, invalid API key, missing parameters, or unauthorized access.
Internal Razorpay server error (HTTP 500) or service temporarily unavailable (HTTP 503).
Request failed due to an error at the downstream bank or payment gateway (HTTP 502).
3D Secure or OTP failed (user cancelled, closed browser, or entered wrong OTP).
Customer exceeded the standard time limit (typically 10 minutes) for payment processing.
Customer cancelled the transaction or pressed the back button during processing.
Issuing bank's Core Banking System encountered technical downtime while processing.
The issuer declined the transaction due to a lack of available funds in the account.
Customer entered an incorrect CVV during the checkout process.
The credit/debit card used has passed its expiration date.
The card has been blocked by the issuing bank or by the customer.
The customer has reached their card's daily transaction or withdrawal limit.
The card is not enrolled for the specific payment method requested.
The specific card network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard) is not enabled for the merchant account.
The network failed to process the transaction using the provided Virtual Payment Address (VPA).
Customer exceeded the maximum transaction volume/limit set by their bank for UPI.
The bank's daily Core Banking System cutoff and reconciliation is actively running.
The selected bank is not currently enabled or active on the UPI network.
Customer's Aadhaar is not linked to their account with the specific biller.
The biller does not accept direct payments without a prior successful "fetch bill" request.
The bill details used are stale or the bill's due date has elapsed.
The Convenience Fee in the payment request doesn't match the fetched bill's required fee.
A request with the same idempotency key has already been processed by the system.
The customer's utility/biller account has been migrated to a different provider.
Order not found, expired, or missing.
Payment gateway unreachable, timeout, or no response from the gateway.
The customer entered an incorrect PIN on the POS terminal.
PIN attempts exceeded.
Insufficient funds (Issuer decline).
Expired card (Issuer decline).
Exceeded usage or withdrawal limit on the card.
EMV Chip card decline (Authorization worked but gateway confirmation failed).
